newsitem.title: FRANCE: French finance minister dismisses probe reports.
newsitem.headline: French finance minister dismisses probe reports.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on radio on Sunday he was surprised by recent press reports that he could be put under investigation in a corruption probe and said that he was not guilty of any wrongdoing.
"I cannot hide the fact that I am amazed by these groundless rumours," Arthuis said. "I do not intend to allow myself to become suspect of something I have nothing to do with."

French investigative weekly Le Canard Enchaine said in March that Arthuis and Labour Minister Jacques Barrot could be placed under investigation by a judge probing illicit funding of the centrist CDS political party.
The Paris public prosecutor's office denied at the time the report that it had been informed of plans by judge Jean-Pierre Zanoto to put the two men under investigation.

Barrot, speaking on a separate radio programme, said he was not losing sleep over the matter and that his role in the party as secretary general was limited to a purely political, rather than financial, one.
Arthuis, who had said little on the matter to date, told RTL he had a clear conscience but was hurt by the impact on family, friends and supporters.
"This affair does not concern me. I am totally serene. But what hurts and bothers me is for my family, those close to me and my friends," he said.
He said political party funding had been a "delicate" issue before clean-up legislation at the end of the 1980s. But, he added, "I was not a party leader, I was not party treasurer."
